features.title: Cargo workspace and gate baseline
features.description: Create the virtual workspace at the repository root with two member crates under crates/: onlypassword-core (lib) and onlypassword-cli (bin named onlypassword). Both set publish = false, edition 2021, carry #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in lib.rs/main.rs, and declare no dependencies yet (later features add approved ones). Each crate root also carries #![cfg_attr(not(test), deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::indexing_slicing))] (not [workspace.lints]). The core crate declares two empty, non-default cargo features, insecure-fast-kdf and test-hooks; the CLI crate never enables them. Add .gitignore for target/. Include one trivial passing test per crate so cargo test runs. Commit Cargo.lock.
acceptance: bash /src/pipeline/gate.sh prints GATE PASSED on the checkout
Cargo.toml is a virtual workspace with members crates/onlypassword-core and crates/onlypassword-cli; Cargo.lock is committed
Both crate roots start with #![forbid(unsafe_code)]
cargo build produces a binary named onlypassword
No dependency appears in any Cargo.toml yet
onlypassword-core/Cargo.toml has [features] insecure-fast-kdf = [] and test-hooks = [] and no `default` entry listing them; onlypassword-cli/Cargo.toml does not enable them
clippy with -D warnings passes on test code that uses unwrap (the deny lints apply only outside cfg(test))

features.title: Error type and secret containers
features.description: Implement the error module (Error enum exactly as in architecture.md, Display with fixed strings, std::error::Error) and the secret module: SecretString and SecretVec/fixed-size secret byte containers that zeroize on drop, have redacted Debug, no Display, no Serialize. Re-export from lib.rs. Adds the zeroize dependency.
acceptance: Error variants carry only &'static str or std::io::ErrorKind; a test shows Display output of every variant is a fixed string containing no input data
format!("{:?}") of a SecretString/SecretVec holding the sentinel 'hunter2-sentinel' does not contain the sentinel and contains 'redacted'
A compile-time assertion (generic fn requiring ZeroizeOnDrop) is instantiated for every secret type
SecretString has no Display, Serialize or implicit Clone to a plain String (reviewer confirms by reading the diff)
Only zeroize is added to dependencies

features.title: OS randomness and unbiased uniform sampling
features.description: Implement the rng module on top of getrandom: fill_random, random_array::<N>() returning Result and mapping failure to Error::Rng, and uniform(n) by rejection sampling exactly as specified in architecture.md. Introduce an internal RandomSource trait so tests can inject a deterministic byte stream. No fallback source of randomness exists.
acceptance: A test with a stubbed RandomSource that returns u64 values from a fixed sequence shows uniform(n) rejects values below 2^64 mod n and returns x % n otherwise (n = 3 and n = 10 and n = 2^63 + 1 cases)

The rejection logic is generic over the raw draw width in an internal helper, and a test runs it with an exhaustive 8-bit source (all 256 inputs) for n = 3 and n = 10 showing exactly equal counts of every residue among accepted draws
uniform(0) returns Err(InvalidInput)
When the RandomSource returns an error, uniform and random_array return Error::Rng; the code contains no other random source (reviewer reads the diff)
Only getrandom is added to dependencies

features.title: Base32 codec
features.description: Implement the base32 module (RFC 4648 section 6 alphabet): encode without padding (upper case), tolerant decode (case-insensitive, ignores ASCII spaces and '-', accepts optional trailing '=' only at the end), strict rejection of everything else including non-zero trailing bits for the unpadded canonical form used by the secret key. Returns Error::InvalidInput on bad input, never panics. Also provides in this module: parse_totp_secret(text) -> SecretVec (tolerant: case-insensitive, ignores spaces and '-', optional trailing '=', 10..=128 decoded bytes) and normalize_totp_secret(text) -> SecretString (the canonical stored form of CS 7: upper case, no padding or separators, trailing bits zero), and a small hex codec (lower-case encode, strict decode) used for ItemId; there is no hex crate.
acceptance: Test loads spec/vectors/base32.json and checks encode (after stripping '=') and decode of every vector
decode rejects: invalid characters, '=' in the middle, odd lengths that cannot occur, and (in strict mode) non-zero trailing bits; each case has a test returning Err
A test feeding 10 000 pseudo-random byte strings (seeded xorshift in the test) to decode never panics
No dependency added
parse_totp_secret accepts lower case, spaces, '-' and trailing '=', returns InvalidInput for invalid characters, an empty secret, 9 decoded bytes and 129 decoded bytes, and accepts 10 and 128

normalize_totp_secret returns upper case without padding or separators ('gezd gnbv-gy3t=' style input gives the canonical text) and is idempotent; the hex codec round-trips and rejects upper case, odd length and non-hex

features.title: AEAD and HKDF primitives with known-answer tests
features.description: Implement crypto::aead (seal/open with XChaCha20-Poly1305: 32-byte key newtype, 24-byte random nonce generated per call and returned with the ciphertext, associated data argument, open returns Error::Authentication and no plaintext on failure, output plaintext in a zeroizing buffer) and crypto::hkdf (extract+expand, and expand-from-PRK with fixed output 32). Also add the shared test helper for loading spec/vectors/*.json via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR. Adds chacha20poly1305, hkdf, sha2, and serde_json (dev use via helper); the helper has its own tiny hex decoder (no hex crate). Integration tests that need nothing else are not gated.
acceptance: KAT: spec/vectors/xchacha20poly1305.json decrypts to the published plaintext and encrypts (with the vector nonce, via an internal deterministic path used only in tests) to the published ciphertext and tag

KAT: spec/vectors/chacha20poly1305.json (RFC 8439 2.8.2) is reproduced by the chacha20poly1305 crate's ChaCha20Poly1305 (test-only use). spec/vectors/hchacha20.json (draft 2.2.1) cannot be exercised through the approved crates (HChaCha20 is internal); it is informational, and the XChaCha20 vector covers HChaCha20 indirectly
KAT: spec/vectors/hkdf-sha256.json test cases A.1-A.3 produce the published OKM
Tamper tests: flipping any bit of ciphertext, tag, nonce or associated data makes open return Error::Authentication; wrong key does too
Two seal calls with identical inputs produce different nonces
KAT helper fails the test when the vector file is missing or contains no vectors
The public seal API cannot be given a caller-chosen nonce outside cfg(test)

features.title: Argon2id key derivation and parameters
features.description: Implement KdfParams (DEFAULT, MIN = the real floor m=19456,t=2,p=1, FAST_FOR_TESTS under cfg(any(test, feature="insecure-fast-kdf")) only, validate with the CS section 10 bounds where the floor drops to FAST_FOR_TESTS only under that cfg, validate_strict always using the real floor), password normalization (UTF-8 of NFKC, minimum 8 scalar values for creation paths via a separate check function), and crypto::kdf::argon2id(password, salt16, params) -> 32-byte secret key material using Argon2id v0x13 with no secret and no associated data (sequential lanes; enable argon2 features alloc and, if available, zeroize; never parallel). Adds argon2 and unicode-normalization.
acceptance: KAT: spec/vectors/argon2id.json (RFC 9106 5.3) reproduces the published tag using the Argon2 library with the vector's secret and associated data (test-only access to those inputs) and the vector's version, memory, passes, lanes

KdfParams::DEFAULT is exactly m=65536, t=3, p=4; MIN is m=19456, t=2, p=1; validate_strict() rejects m<19456, m>262144, t<2, t>16, p=0, p>16 and accepts the boundary values; with the fast cfg, validate() additionally accepts FAST_FOR_TESTS (8192,1,1) but still rejects m<8192
Validation happens before Argon2 runs (a test with m = u32::MAX returns Err quickly)
Normalization fixed results from CS 3.1: U+0065 U+0301 -> C3 A9, U+FB01 -> 66 69, U+00B5 -> CE BC, U+FF11 -> 31
Password check rejects empty and 7-scalar-value passwords and accepts 8, counted after normalization
One test derives with DEFAULT params and finishes (smoke)
A test run under --all-features still asserts the real floor through validate_strict

features.title: Secret key and key hierarchy
features.description: Implement crypto::keys: SecretKey (generate, to_text, from_text per CS 3.2, built on the base32 module, plus from_key_file_text that trims ASCII whitespace at both ends first and rejects a BOM), MasterKey derivation (Argon2id output plus secret key through HKDF with INFO_MK exactly as CS 3.3), VaultKey (random), ItemKey (random), subkeys K_iw and K_fa from VaultKey via HKDF-Expand with the CS 3.5 labels. All key newtypes zeroize on drop, redact Debug, are not Copy.
acceptance: SecretKey text round trip; output starts with 'OPSK1-', has 13 groups of 4 characters after the prefix separated by '-'
from_text rejects wrong prefix, wrong length, invalid characters, non-zero trailing bits (each a test returning Err(InvalidInput)) and accepts lower case and extra spaces
Master key derivation test: same password+salt+params+secret key gives the same key; changing any one of them gives a different key; password-only and secret-key-only changes are both detected
A test recomputes MasterKey independently in the test using the hkdf and argon2 crates directly with info 'onlypassword/v1/master-key' and salt = kdf_salt, IKM = pw_key || SK, and compares
Subkeys K_iw and K_fa differ from each other and from VK; labels are exactly those in CS 3.5 (test recomputes via hkdf)
All key types implement ZeroizeOnDrop (compile-time assertion) and Debug prints no key bytes (sentinel test)
Uses KdfParams::FAST_FOR_TESTS in tests for speed
from_key_file_text accepts the text with a trailing newline, leading spaces and CRLF, and returns InvalidInput for a leading BOM and for text with interior garbage

features.title: Item model and versioned serialization
features.description: Implement the item module: Item, ItemKind, TotpConfig, TotpAlgorithm, CustomField, ItemId (hex Display/FromStr using the F004 hex codec, random generation), validation of every limit and kind rule in CS section 7 (including the canonical TOTP secret rule: upper-case base32, no padding, 10..=128 decoded bytes), and JSON serialization/deserialization of the schema-1 plaintext exactly as CS section 7: compact, fixed key order, written into a Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> with preallocated capacity; read in two passes (probe the 'schema' key first: != 1 is UnsupportedVersion, before anything else; then a strict pass with deny_unknown_fields structs, no serde(default), no flatten, duplicate keys rejected, and the nullable keys username/password/totp REQUIRED to be present via deserialize_with or a wrapper type). Secret fields are SecretString; Debug redacts them. Adds serde (derive) and serde_json to core.
acceptance: Round-trip test for a login with every field populated and for a note

Deserializing JSON with an unknown field, a duplicate key (at top level, inside totp and inside a fields[] entry), a missing field (one test row per required key, including username, password and totp ABSENT while the other keys are present), a wrong type, a note with a password, a title of 0 or 1025 bytes, 65 URLs, 257 custom fields, totp digits 5 or 9, period 0 or 301, and a plaintext over 1 MiB each returns Corrupt (or InvalidInput for the size limit) and never panics; schema 0 or 2 returns UnsupportedVersion, also when the same object has unknown fields; a missing, duplicate or non-integer schema returns Corrupt

Item::validate rejects the same violations on the construction side with InvalidInput, and additionally a TOTP secret that is lower case, padded, contains spaces or '-', decodes to 9 or 129 bytes, or has non-zero trailing bits
Serialized output for a fixed item matches the key names and types in CS section 7 (test parses the JSON as serde_json::Value and checks keys)
ItemId display is 32 lowercase hex chars; FromStr rejects upper case, wrong length and non-hex
Debug of Item containing a password 'hunter2-sentinel' does not contain it; custom field values and TOTP secrets likewise
Serialization of a fixed item equals the expected byte string with keys in the CS section 7 order, compact, and serializing twice gives identical bytes

features.title: Vault file byte codec
features.description: Implement the format module: a pure, key-free codec for the vault file of CS section 5. Parse bytes into Header/Records/Trailer and serialize back deterministically, using a bounds-checked reader (no indexing, checked arithmetic). Enforce the vault-file check table of CS 9 steps 1-7 (length, magic -> Corrupt, format_version -> UnsupportedVersion, flags -> Corrupt, kdf_id/kdf_version -> UnsupportedVersion, KDF bounds including the floor via KdfParams::validate -> Corrupt, structure -> Corrupt) and the limits of CS 10 before allocating. Records must be strictly ascending by item_id.
acceptance: Layout test builds a vault image by hand from the offsets in CS section 5 (header 130 bytes, record fixed part 126, trailer 40) and the parser reads every field correctly; serialize(parse(x)) == x

format_version 0, 2 and 0xFFFF return UnsupportedVersion; kdf_id != 1 and kdf_version != 0x13 return UnsupportedVersion; flags != 0, each KDF parameter outside bounds (floor and ceiling), record_len/body_ct_len mismatch, record_count larger than the data allows, record_count > 100000, unsorted or duplicate item_ids, trailing or missing trailer bytes, truncation at every length from 0 to full each return Err(Corrupt) without panic; a test with several faults at once (version 2 AND bad flags) shows the first failing step of the CS 9 table decides the error

A file claiming record_count = 4 294 967 295 or a record_len of 4 GiB is rejected without allocating more than the input length (test uses a small buffer and asserts Err; reviewer confirms Vec::with_capacity is never fed an untrusted count)
An export-file magic given to the vault parser returns Err(Corrupt)
No unwrap/expect/panic/indexing on parsed data in non-test code (reviewer confirms by reading the diff)

features.title: Sealing: header wrap, item records, file trailer
features.description: Implement the seal module joining crypto and format: wrap/unwrap VK with AD_VK over the header prefix; seal_item/open_item producing/consuming records with a fresh IK and nonces and the AD_IK/AD_BODY of CS 6.3; compute and verify the trailer tag over SHA-256 of the file prefix with K_fa (CS 6.4). The unwrap-and-verify-trailer step must complete before any record is decrypted. Adds nothing beyond approved crates.
acceptance: Seal then open round-trips an item; the same item sealed twice yields different nonces, IK wrapping and ciphertext
Flipping any single byte of a sealed vault image (every offset, one at a time, header through trailer) makes either open_vault/verify or open_item return an error and never returns plaintext
A record copied onto a different item_id, a different revision, a different vault_id, or with item_schema/format_version changed fails with Authentication
Deleting a record, adding a record sealed under the same keys, or replacing a record with an older valid revision of the same item makes trailer verification fail with Authentication
Wrong MK returns Authentication from unwrap_vk; a header whose KDF params were edited returns Authentication or Corrupt
AD byte strings are built as in CS 6.2-6.4: a test builds AD_VK, AD_IK, AD_BODY, AD_FILE independently from the layout and decrypts a sealed record with the AEAD crate directly
No record is decrypted when the trailer fails (test with a record sealed by a different VK and a counter showing zero decrypt attempts, or a structural equivalent)

A record whose item_schema field is changed (and the trailer recomputed with the right K_fa so only the record-level check is exercised) fails with Authentication, never UnsupportedVersion; a body sealed with item_schema 1 whose JSON schema is 2 is UnsupportedVersion on open_item, and one whose JSON schema is 1 while the record item_schema is 2 (sealed that way) is Corrupt

features.title: Atomic file storage
features.description: Implement the storage module (CS 6.6): write_atomic(path, bytes) creating a uniquely named temporary file in the target's directory with create_new (0600 on Unix via std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt), write_all, sync_all, rename over the target, then fsync the directory on Unix; if the target is a symlink resolve it first (fs::canonicalize) and write next to and rename over the resolved file; remove the temp file on any failure. create_new_atomic(path, bytes) for new vaults: write the temp file the same way, std::fs::hard_link(temp, target) (fails if the target exists), remove the temp file, fsync the directory; no rename fallback (Io if hard links are unsupported); a pub(crate) hook between the temp write and the link is available to unit tests. read_bounded(path, max) refuses files above the limit before reading everything. same_file_path(a, b) compares canonicalized paths (canonical parent plus file name for a non-existent target). Adds tempfile as a dev-dependency.
acceptance: After write_atomic over an existing file the new content is present and no temp file remains in the directory
When the rename step fails (target path is a directory) the function returns Err(Io), the old content is untouched and no temp file remains
A test that makes the directory unwritable (Unix, skipped by cfg on other platforms rather than ignored) leaves the target unchanged
On Unix a newly created file has mode 0600 (test checks metadata)

create_new_atomic on an existing path returns an error and leaves the file's content unchanged; with the hook creating the target between the temp write and the link, create_new_atomic fails, the hook-created file is byte-identical afterwards and no temp file remains; a hook that aborts before the link (simulated crash) leaves no file at the target; new files have mode 0600
read_bounded returns Err(LimitExceeded) for a file larger than the maximum without reading it fully
Io errors map to Error::Io(kind) with no path or message
write_atomic on a path that is a symlink to a file (Unix, cfg-gated) updates the file and leaves the symlink in place
same_file_path reports true for the same file reached through a symlink or a dotted path, and for a not-yet-existing target in the same directory with the same name

features.title: Vault create, unlock, lock
features.description: Implement Vault::create_with_key, Vault::create, Vault::unlock, Vault::lock, Vault::kdf_params and the Clock trait/SystemClock (set_clock only under cfg(test) or feature test-hooks, #[doc(hidden)]). create_with_key(path, password, params, &SecretKey) generates salt, vault_id and VK, wraps VK, and writes an empty valid vault through storage::create_new_atomic; create generates the SecretKey and calls it and returns (Vault, SecretKey). unlock follows the CS 9 order: read_bounded, parse, derive MK, unwrap VK, verify trailer. Wrong password and wrong secret key return the same Error::Authentication. Vault zeroizes its keys on drop; lock consumes the vault.
acceptance: create then unlock with the returned secret key succeeds; the file starts with the 8-byte magic and has length 130 + 4 + 40 for an empty vault

create and create_with_key at an existing path return an error and the existing file's bytes are unchanged, including when the target appears between the temp write and the publication (hook); create with a crash simulated before the link leaves no vault
create rejects a password shorter than 8 scalar values and KDF params outside bounds (validate_strict floor outside the fast cfg) with InvalidInput before touching the disk
unlock with a wrong password and with a wrong secret key both return Error::Authentication (equal values); unlock of a nonexistent path returns Io
The secret key text never appears in the vault file bytes (test scans the file for the key bytes and for the text)
lock(self) consumes the vault (compile-fail is not required; a doc comment and signature show it); Vault implements ZeroizeOnDrop-equivalent behavior and its Debug is redacted
Unlock of a file with any single flipped byte returns Err (loop over every offset, FAST_FOR_TESTS)
create_with_key then unlock with the SAME key succeeds and Vault::kdf_params returns the params used
unlock applies no password-length minimum (a vault created through a test seam with a short password still reports Authentication, not InvalidInput, for a wrong short password)

features.title: Item operations: add, get, update, delete, list, search
features.description: Add Vault::add/get/update/delete/list/search. Each mutation builds a complete new file image, writes it atomically, and only then updates the in-memory state. add assigns a random ItemId (retry on the astronomically unlikely collision), revision 1 and created_ms = updated_ms = clock; update bumps revision, keeps created_ms, sets updated_ms to max(now, created_ms), uses a new item key and nonces. list returns summaries sorted by title.to_lowercase() (byte-wise) then id bytes. search lower-cases query and fields with str::to_lowercase and tests contains. Every mutation checks the CS 10 limits (512 MiB image, 100000 records) before writing and returns LimitExceeded; update on an item whose revision is u64::MAX returns LimitExceeded (checked before incrementing).
acceptance: Add three items, lock, unlock, get each: contents and revision 1 equal the originals; created_ms == updated_ms from an injected test Clock
update: revision becomes 2, created_ms unchanged, updated_ms equals the new clock value, the old and new record bytes differ in item key and nonces; update/delete/get of an unknown id return NotFound
delete removes the item; get returns NotFound and list no longer shows it; the file survives lock/unlock
list is sorted by lower-case title then id and summaries expose no password, notes, TOTP secret or hidden field value (struct has no such fields)
search finds by substring of title, username and URL in any case, and does not match a substring that exists only in a password, note, TOTP secret or custom field
Invalid items (CS 7 violations) return InvalidInput and leave the file bytes unchanged
Failure injection: when the target directory is made read-only (Unix) a mutation returns Err(Io) and both file bytes and in-memory get/list results are unchanged
Two items are never given the same ItemId in a test adding 1000 items with KdfParams::FAST_FOR_TESTS
Non-ASCII ordering and search: titles 'Éclair', 'eclair', 'Σigma', 'İstanbul' sort by str::to_lowercase byte order then id, and search 'σ' finds 'Σigma' (expected order written out in the test)

With the limit constants overridden under cfg(test): add beyond the item limit and an image beyond the size limit return LimitExceeded and leave the file bytes and in-memory state unchanged (the revision u64::MAX case is tested in F018 where import can create it)

features.title: Change master password and rotate vault key
features.description: Add Vault::change_master_password (verify current password and key by deriving and unwrapping, then new salt, new params (validated), new nonce, rewrap the same VK under the new MK, keep every record byte-identical, recompute the trailer) and Vault::rotate_vault_key (new VK, new subkeys, every record re-sealed with a fresh IK and nonces, revisions and contents unchanged, new wrapped_vk under the current MK, recomputed trailer). Also add Vault::change_master_password_and_rotate_key (verify current password and key; new salt, params, new VK, every record re-sealed, wrapped_vk under the NEW master key, one atomic write). Both persist atomically and leave the old state on any failure. The doc comment of change_master_password states that it does not revoke earlier knowledge of the vault key and points to the combined operation.
acceptance: After change_master_password the new password unlocks and the old one returns Authentication; item records region is byte-identical before and after; kdf_salt and vk_nonce differ; changing to the same password still changes salt and nonce
change_master_password with a wrong current password returns Authentication and changes nothing; new password under 8 scalar values returns InvalidInput; new params out of bounds return InvalidInput

After rotate_vault_key all items read back identical (including revisions); every record's wrapped_ik, body_nonce and body ciphertext differ from before; the old file copy's bytes cannot be unlocked as part of the new file (splicing an old record into the new file fails trailer verification)
A test holding the old VK (from before rotation) cannot open any record of the new file
A simulated write failure during either operation leaves the previous file and in-memory state usable
Header vault_id and the secret key are unchanged by both operations

change_master_password_and_rotate_key: the new password unlocks, the old fails with Authentication, all items read back identical, every record differs from before, the old VK cannot open any record, and a failure injected at the write leaves the previous file usable; the doc comment on change_master_password mentions rotation (test greps the source doc string)

features.title: Random password generator
features.description: Implement generator::generate_password and PasswordOptions per architecture.md: classes, ambiguous exclusion, require_each, uniform sampling, Fisher-Yates shuffle through the RandomSource trait. Return SecretString. The public generate_password uses the OS source; unit tests (inside the crate) call a pub(crate) generate_password_with(&mut dyn RandomSource, &PasswordOptions).
acceptance: Default options give 20 characters from the four classes with at least one of each

Every option combination test: length 4 to 256 accepted, 3 and 257 rejected with InvalidInput; no class enabled, an enabled class that becomes empty after exclusion (impossible with the fixed sets; test via a zero-class case), and length < number of required classes all return InvalidInput
exclude_ambiguous output never contains any of 0 O o 1 l I over 1000 generated passwords

With the deterministic RandomSource stub the output is reproducible and a frequency test over a large simulated sample shows each character of the union appears with equal frequency (+/- statistical tolerance chosen so the test is deterministic)
When the RandomSource fails the function returns Error::Rng
The generated password type is SecretString and its Debug is redacted

features.title: Word-based passphrase generator
features.description: Implement generator::generate_passphrase and PassphraseOptions using the 2048-word English list from the bip39 crate (Language::English.word_list()). Uniform word choice through uniform(2048), separator (at most 8 ASCII chars), optional capitalization of each word's first letter, optional single digit appended to one uniformly chosen word. Adds bip39 with the fewest features that expose the word list and never the rand feature; the chosen feature set is recorded in agent-notes/. The public generate_passphrase uses the OS source; unit tests call a pub(crate) generate_passphrase_with(&mut dyn RandomSource, ..). Capitalize ASCII-upper-cases the first byte of each word.
acceptance: Default produces 7 words joined by '-', every word is in the bip39 English list (test checks membership)
Words 4 to 24 accepted; 3 and 25 rejected; separator longer than 8 or containing non-ASCII rejected, all InvalidInput
capitalize makes each word start upper case; include_digit yields exactly one ASCII digit appended to exactly one word
With the stub RandomSource, word indices are unbiased (2048 is a power of two; test checks uniform(2048) uses no rejection and that the stub's draws map to the expected words)
The word list has exactly 2048 distinct entries (test)
Failure of the RandomSource returns Error::Rng

features.title: HOTP and TOTP
features.description: Implement the totp module: hotp (RFC 4226 section 5.3 dynamic truncation) and totp (RFC 6238, time as an explicit argument, T = floor(unix_secs / period)) for SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512 via the hmac, sha1, sha2 crates; re-uses parse_totp_secret from the F004 base32 module (10..=128 byte rule) and rejects TotpConfig secrets that fail normalization; totp_for_item(&TotpConfig, unix_secs). Zero digits formatting with leading zeros. Parameters out of range return InvalidInput. No clock access inside the module.
acceptance: KAT: every row of spec/vectors/totp.json (all three algorithms, 18 rows) matches using the row's secret_hex, 8 digits, period 30
KAT: every count of spec/vectors/hotp.json matches with 6 digits
KAT: spec/vectors/hmac-sha2.json cases match the HMAC-SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-512 implementation used
KAT: spec/vectors/hmac-sha1.json (RFC 2202 cases 1-4) match the HMAC-SHA-1 implementation used
Leading zeros are preserved (the 07081804 row)
digits 5 and 9, period 0 and 301, an empty secret, a 9-byte secret and a 129-byte secret return InvalidInput
parse_totp_secret accepts lower case, spaces, '-' and trailing '=' and rejects invalid characters
totp does not call SystemTime (reviewer confirms by grep in the diff)

features.title: Encrypted export and import
features.description: Implement the export module and Vault::export(path, export_password, &SecretKey, params) / Vault::import(path, export_password, &SecretKey source_key) per CS section 8 and the export table of CS 9: export header (74 bytes), Argon2id from the export password with fresh salt, HKDF INFO_EXPORT over export_pw_key || SK, AEAD with AD_X over the header, compact JSON payload (fixed key order, items sorted by id with revisions, exported_ms from the vault clock) read in two passes like items; written atomically with write_atomic; export rejects a target equal to the vault file (same_file_path) with InvalidInput and returns LimitExceeded rather than a payload over MAX_EXPORT_PLAINTEXT. import follows the CS 9 export table in order, bounds ct_len before allocating, decrypts, validates every item (sorted unique ids, <= 100000 items, CS 7 rules), checks all IDs against the vault (Conflict if any exists) and the CS 10 limits (LimitExceeded), and writes the vault once. The export password minimum applies to export only, not to import. The target vault keeps its own vault_id; items keep their ids and revisions.
acceptance: Export vault A (several items incl. a note and a login with TOTP and custom fields) with A's key, create fresh vault B with a DIFFERENT secret key, import with A's key as source_key: B.list() equals A.list() and get of every id equals A's (contents, revision, timestamps)

Wrong export password returns Authentication; wrong source_key (B's own key) returns the same Authentication; B is unchanged both times; flipping any single byte of the export file (loop over all offsets) returns an error from import and B is unchanged

A test derives K_x independently (hkdf and argon2 crates directly, IKM = export_pw_key || SK, info 'onlypassword/v1/export-key', AD_X over file[0..74]) and decrypts an exported file with the AEAD crate

Export header layout test: 74 bytes, magic OPEXPORT, ct_len equals file length minus 74; the error table of CS 9: format_version 0/2 -> UnsupportedVersion, flags != 0 -> Corrupt, kdf_id/kdf_version wrong -> UnsupportedVersion, KDF params below the floor -> Corrupt, ct_len mismatch -> Corrupt, and a payload sealed with export_schema 2 (or an item schema 2) -> UnsupportedVersion after successful decryption (sealed in a unit test with the internal API)
Importing into a vault that already has one of the ids returns Conflict and imports nothing (list unchanged, file bytes unchanged)
The export file bytes contain neither the secret key bytes/text nor any plaintext field value used in the test (scan)
A file claiming ct_len = u64::MAX or a length mismatching the file returns Corrupt without large allocation; truncations at every length return Err

Export password under 8 scalar values returns InvalidInput on export but import with a short export password reaches Authentication/decryption (no InvalidInput); two exports of the same vault differ (fresh salt and nonce); export failure leaves any existing target file unchanged
export with --out equal to the vault path (also via a symlink to it, Unix) returns InvalidInput and the vault is unchanged

An item imported with revision u64::MAX (exported from a unit-test-built payload) is readable, and update on it returns LimitExceeded without writing; import that would exceed the item-count limit (constants overridden under cfg(test)) returns LimitExceeded and imports nothing

features.title: CLI: parser, prompts, init, note and read commands
features.description: Build the onlypassword binary: hand-written argument parser (global --vault, --secret-key-file, --stdin; unknown flags are usage errors), a prompt module (rpassword no-echo, or stdin lines with --stdin, confirm prompts), exit-code mapping (0, 1, 2, 3), key-file reading (SecretKey::from_key_file_text) and the commands init, add-note, get, list, search, delete as in architecture.md section 5. init follows the section 5 'init order' exactly: check both paths do not exist and differ, generate the key, create the key file with create_new and 0600 and sync, read it back and compare, Vault::create_with_key, remove the key file if vault creation fails; it does not print the key unless --print-secret-key. add-note takes exactly one of --notes (prompt switch) or --notes-file. get prints <hidden> for password, notes, TOTP secret and hidden fields unless --show-secrets. Adds rpassword (and zeroize in the cli crate).
acceptance: Integration tests run the real binary (env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_onlypassword")) with --stdin in a temp dir: init, add-note (with --notes prompt and with --notes-file), list, search, get, delete behave as specified and print IDs and tab-separated list lines

get output contains '<hidden>' for the password, notes, TOTP secret and hidden fields and never their values; with --show-secrets it contains them (the item for this test is inserted through the core library in the test)

init order tests: an existing key file, a missing key-file directory, an existing vault path, key-file path equal to vault path, and an unwritable vault directory (step 6 failing) each exit 1 and leave no new file behind and never touch an existing one; after a successful init the key file mode is 0600 on Unix, unlock with the key file works, and the secret key text is not in stdout or stderr without --print-secret-key
Wrong password exits 3 with a one-line message that does not contain the password; a missing stdin line, unknown flag or missing --vault exits 2; unknown item id exits 1
No secret is accepted from argv or environment (reviewer reads the parser; a test shows --password and --notes=TEXT are rejected as usage errors)
A key file with a trailing newline, CRLF or surrounding spaces works; a key file with a BOM or garbage exits 1 without printing its content
No panic on empty argv, unknown commands, or invalid UTF-8 arguments (test via OsString)

features.title: CLI: add-login and update with the full item model
features.description: Add add-login and update with every item flag of architecture.md section 5: --title/--username/--url, prompt switches --notes, --new-password, --totp, hidden field values, --notes-file, --generate, --totp-algorithm/--totp-digits/--totp-period (only with --totp), --field NAME=VALUE and --hidden-field NAME (prompted in command-line order), and on update the --clear-username/--clear-urls/--clear-notes/--clear-totp/--clear-fields flags with the replace semantics stated there. TOTP secrets are stored through normalize_totp_secret. The prompt order is: master, item password, TOTP secret, notes, hidden values.
acceptance: add-login with --totp --totp-digits 8 --totp-period 30 --totp-algorithm sha1, one --field and two --hidden-field flags, --notes and prompted values in the documented order stores exactly those values (verified with get --show-secrets and, for the TOTP fields, with the core library in the test)

add-login without TOTP flags stores sha1/6/30 when --totp is given; --totp-digits without --totp is a usage error (exit 2); --generate stores a generated password that is not printed without --show-secrets and is shown by get --show-secrets

update: unmentioned fields unchanged; --url replaces the list; --field/--hidden-field replace the field list; each --clear-* flag clears; a clear flag plus a setter for the same field exits 2; update with --notes-file replaces notes; unknown id exits 1; a flag illegal for a note (e.g. --username on a note) exits 1 with no change
A pasted lower-case, spaced TOTP secret on the prompt is stored in canonical form; an invalid TOTP secret exits 1 and nothing is stored
argv of every command in these tests contains no secret value (the test asserts that notes, passwords and hidden values were supplied only through stdin or a notes file)

features.title: CLI: passwd, rotate-key, export, import, generate, totp
features.description: Add the remaining commands to the CLI: passwd [--rotate] (rotate calls change_master_password_and_rotate_key; without it print a reminder that the vault key was not rotated), rotate-key, export --out (uses the global --secret-key-file as the export key; rejects an --out equal to --vault with exit 2), import --in --source-secret-key-file, totp <ID> [--time], generate password and generate passphrase with their flags (no vault or key needed). Use the same prompt order as architecture.md section 5. totp prints the code and the seconds remaining in the period using the system clock (or --time).
acceptance: Tests drive the real binary: passwd then unlock with the new password works and the old password exits 3; passwd --rotate additionally changes every record (bytes differ) and list/get output stays identical; rotate-key keeps list/get output identical

export then import into a freshly initialised vault (new key file) with --source-secret-key-file pointing at the old key file reproduces list and get --show-secrets output; import with the new vault's own key file as source exits 3 and changes nothing
export --out equal to --vault exits 2 and the vault is unchanged

totp --time 59 for an item whose secret is the RFC 6238 SHA-1 seed in base32 (GEZDGNBVGY3TQOJQGEZDGNBVGY3TQOJQ) with 8 digits and period 30 (added through add-login --totp --totp-digits 8) prints 94287082 (value from spec/vectors/totp.json)

generate password --length 32 --no-symbols prints 32 alphanumeric characters; generate passphrase --words 5 --separator '.' prints 5 words separated by '.'; invalid values (--length 3, --words 2) exit 2
export to an existing --out path replaces it atomically through the core, and a failed export leaves the old file intact
import with a wrong export password exits 3 and the vault is unchanged

features.title: Hostile-input robustness suite
features.description: Add integration tests (no production code unless a bug is found) that feed hostile input to every untrusted-input parser through the public API: vault files, export files, item JSON through unlock/get, secret key text, TOTP secrets and generator options. Use a seeded xorshift generator written in the test; no new dependency. Fix any panic or unbounded allocation found, in the owning module, with a regression test.
acceptance: For a small valid vault and a small valid export file: every truncation length, every single-byte flip, and 2000 seeded random mutations (flip, insert, delete, overwrite a 4-byte length field with 0, u32::MAX, u64::MAX) are fed to unlock/import: each returns Err or (for mutations that cannot matter) never returns wrong plaintext, and none panics or takes over 5 seconds (FAST_FOR_TESTS)
2000 seeded random garbage buffers of sizes 0 to 4096 and buffers beginning with each valid magic produce Err without panic for unlock and import
SecretKey::from_text and parse_totp_secret and ItemId::from_str receive 5000 seeded random strings including non-ASCII and very long (1 MiB) inputs without panic

A vault with a deliberately huge declared record_count or length fields (header fixed up) is rejected without large allocation (test asserts completion with a memory-bounded buffer, e.g. input < 1 KiB)

Authenticated-but-invalid content: a record whose decrypted JSON is invalid or has an unknown field returns Corrupt from get; JSON schema 2 (also with an unknown field) returns UnsupportedVersion; an absent nullable key returns Corrupt (a unit test inside the core crate seals such a body with the internal seal API)
Reviewer confirms by diff that no #[ignore] and no catch_unwind hides a panic

features.title: End-to-end CLI test (definition of done)
features.description: Add crates/onlypassword-cli/tests/e2e.rs, a single scenario test driving the real onlypassword binary with default KDF parameters: init a vault; add several items (login with TOTP and custom fields, login with generated password, secure note); lock (process exit) and unlock by running read commands again; read every item back and compare to what was added; change the master password with passwd --rotate (old fails with exit 3, new works); export; init a fresh vault with a new key file; import with --source-secret-key-file set to the first vault's key file; verify list and get --show-secrets output are identical to the first vault. Also assert negative end states: wrong secret key exits 3, tampered vault byte exits non-zero.
acceptance: The scenario test passes under the gate and takes a bounded time (default Argon2 parameters, a few dozen invocations)
Every step of the brief's definition of done appears in the test in order: create vault, add items, lock, unlock, read back, change master password, export, import into fresh vault
No password, key or secret appears in any captured stdout/stderr except from get --show-secrets and generate (test scans captures for the master, new and export passwords and the key text)
A copy of the vault file with one byte flipped makes the CLI exit non-zero with no plaintext on stdout
Test data uses obviously fake values (e.g. 'correct-horse-test-only') and no real data (REQ-BLD-003)
The import step uses the first vault's key file as --source-secret-key-file, and importing with the second vault's own key file exits 3
